question: Which union territory was established in 1966? (RPF Constable 2024 (06/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: Andaman and Nicobar Islands
Chandigarh
Goa
Delhi
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Chandigarh

Explanation:
The formation of union territories in India occurred due to various administrative needs. Chandigarh was established as a union territory on 1 November 1966, following the reorganisation of Punjab. It serves as the capital of both Punjab and Haryana. The Andaman and Nicobar Islands became a union territory in 1956, while Goa was formed in 1962 after liberation from Portuguese rule in 1961, later becoming a state in 1987. Delhi has been a union territory since 1956 and was designated as the National Capital Territory in 1991. Therefore, the union territory established in 1966 is Chandigarh.

question_hi: कौन सा केंद्र शासित प्रदेश 1966 में स्थापित हुआ था? (RPF Constable 2024 (06/03/2025) Shift 3)

चंडीगढ़
गोवा
दिल्ली
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है चंडीगढ़

Explanation:
भारत में केंद्र शासित प्रदेशों का गठन विभिन्न प्रशासनिक आवश्यकताओं के कारण हुआ। चंडीगढ़ को 1 नवंबर 1966 को केंद्र शासित प्रदेश बनाया गया, जब पंजाब का पुनर्गठन हुआ। यह पंजाब और हरियाणा दोनों की राजधानी है। अंडमान और निकोबार द्वीप समूह 1956 में केंद्र शासित प्रदेश बना, जबकि गोवा 1961 में पुर्तगाल से मुक्त होने के बाद 1962 में बनाया गया और बाद में 1987 में राज्य बना। दिल्ली 1956 से केंद्र शासित प्रदेश है और 1991 में राष्ट्रीय राजधानी क्षेत्र बना। इस प्रकार, 1966 में स्थापित केंद्र शासित प्रदेश चंडीगढ़ है।

question: The right to work is mentioned under _____ of the Indian Constitution. (RPF Constable 2024 (07/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: Article 38
Article 41
Article 39
Article 40
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 41

Explanation:
The right to work is mentioned under Article 41 of the Indian Constitution. This article directs the state to secure the right to work, education, and public assistance in certain cases, such as unemployment, old age, sickness, and disability. It is part of Part IV (Directive Principles of State Policy) and is non-justiciable, meaning it cannot be enforced by courts. Article 41 specifically instructs the state to make effective provision for securing the right to work, the right to education, and the right to public assistance. Other options: Article 38 relates to social welfare, Article 39 relates to policy principles, and Article 40 relates to the organization of village panchayats.

☛ Article 41 belongs to which part? → Part IV (Directive Principles of State Policy)
☛ Is Article 41 justiciable or non-justiciable? → Non-justiciable
☛ What does Article 38 deal with? → Social welfare
☛ What does Article 40 deal with? → Organization of village panchayats
question_hi: भारतीय संविधान के _____ में काम करने के अधिकार का उल्लेख किया गया है। (RPF Constable 2024 (07/03/2025) Shift 1)
options_hi: अनुच्छेद 38
अनुच्छेद 41
अनुच्छेद 39
अनुच्छेद 40
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है अनुच्छेद 41

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 41 में काम करने के अधिकार का उल्लेख किया गया है। यह अनुच्छेद राज्य को निर्देश देता है कि वह कुछ मामलों में, जैसे शिक्षा, रोजगार और सार्वजनिक सहायता के अधिकार को सुरक्षित करे। यह संविधान के भाग IV (राज्य के नीति निदेशक तत्व) में आता है और न्यायोचित नहीं है, अर्थात इसका उल्लंघन होने पर अदालत में याचिका नहीं की जा सकती। अनुच्छेद 41 राज्य को विशेष रूप से काम करने के अधिकार, शिक्षा के अधिकार और बेरोजगारी, बुढ़ापा, बीमारी जैसी स्थितियों में सार्वजनिक सहायता के अधिकार को सुनिश्चित करने का निर्देश देता है। अन्य विकल्प: अनुच्छेद 38 समाज कल्याण, अनुच्छेद 39 नीति सिद्धांत, और अनुच्छेद 40 ग्राम पंचायतों से संबंधित हैं।

question: With respect to the Indian Constitution, the Fundamental Rights are: (RPF Constable 2024 (07/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: written in the Schedules of the Constitution
written in the Constitution
not written in the Constitution
not written in the Schedules nor outside the Schedules of the Constitution
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is written in the Constitution

Explanation:
The Fundamental Rights in the Indian Constitution are explicitly mentioned in Part III (Articles 12-35). These rights guarantee citizens a just and free life. They include the Right to Equality (Articles 14-18), Right to Freedom (Articles 19-22), Right against Exploitation (Articles 23-24), Right to Freedom of Religion (Articles 25-28), Cultural and Educational Rights (Articles 29-30), and Right to Constitutional Remedies (Article 32). These rights are part of the main text of the Constitution, not the Schedules. Hence, option 2 is correct.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ In which Part of the Constitution are Fundamental Rights present? → Part III
☛ Which Articles cover Right to Equality? → 14-18
☛ Which Article covers Right to Constitutional Remedies? → 32
☛ Where are Fundamental Rights described? → Main text of Constitution
☛ Which Articles cover Right to Freedom? → 19-22
question_hi: भारतीय संविधान के संदर्भ में, मौलिक अधिकार हैं: (RPF Constable 2024 (07/03/2025) Shift 1)
options_hi: संविधान के अनुसूचियों में लिखे गए हैं
संविधान में लिखे गए हैं
संविधान में नहीं लिखे गए हैं
न तो संविधान की अनुसूचियों में और न ही अनुसूचियों के बाहर लिखे गए हैं
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है संविधान में लिखे गए हैं

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान के भाग III (अनुच्छेद 12-35) में मौलिक अधिकार स्पष्ट रूप से वर्णित हैं। ये अधिकार नागरिकों को न्यायोचित और स्वतंत्र जीवन जीने की गारंटी देते हैं। इनमें समानता का अधिकार (अनुच्छेद 14-18), स्वतंत्रता का अधिकार (अनुच्छेद 19-22), शोषण के विरुद्ध अधिकार (अनुच्छेद 23-24), धार्मिक स्वतंत्रता का अधिकार (अनुच्छेद 25-28), संस्कृति और शिक्षा का अधिकार (अनुच्छेद 29-30), और संवैधानिक उपचारों का अधिकार (अनुच्छेद 32) शामिल हैं। ये अधिकार संविधान के मुख्य पाठ का हिस्सा हैं, न कि अनुसूचियों का। अतः विकल्प 2 सही है।

question: The Fifth Schedule of the Indian Constitution deals with ____________. (RPF Constable 2024 (07/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: powers of panchayats
administration and control of scheduled areas and scheduled tribes
disqualification on ground of defection
provisions regarding languages
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is administration and control of scheduled areas and scheduled tribes

Explanation:
The Fifth Schedule of the Indian Constitution deals with the administration and control of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes. It comes under Article 244(1) and empowers the Governor to modify or exempt laws in Scheduled Areas. The Sixth Schedule pertains to tribal areas in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram. Powers of Panchayats are covered by the 73rd Amendment (Article 243). Disqualification on ground of defection is in the Tenth Schedule. Provisions regarding languages are in the Eighth Schedule. The Fifth Schedule aims to protect the interests of Scheduled Tribes and ensure their welfare through special administrative measures.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Which states are under the Fifth Schedule? → Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Odisha, Rajasthan, and Telangana.
☛ What is the main objective of the Fifth Schedule? → Protection of Scheduled Tribes' interests and administration of their areas.
☛ Who notifies Scheduled Areas? → The President of India.
☛ Under which article is the Tribal Advisory Council provided in the Fifth Schedule? → Article 244(1).
☛ What special power does the Governor have under the Fifth Schedule? → He can modify or exempt central or state laws in Scheduled Areas.
question_hi: भारतीय संविधान की पाँचवीं अनुसूची किससे संबंधित है? (RPF Constable 2024 (07/03/2025) Shift 1)

दल-बदल के आधार पर अयोग्यता
भाषाओं के संबंध में प्रावधान

Solution: सही उत्तर है अनुसूचित क्षेत्रों और अनुसूचित जनजातियों का प्रशासन और नियंत्रण

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान की पाँचवीं अनुसूची अनुसूचित क्षेत्रों और अनुसूचित जनजातियों के प्रशासन और नियंत्रण से संबंधित है। यह अनुसूची अनुच्छेद 244(1) के तहत आती है और इसमें राज्यपाल को अनुसूचित क्षेत्रों में कानूनों में संशोधन या अपवाद बनाने की शक्ति प्रदान की गई है। छठी अनुसूची असम, मेघालय, त्रिपुरा और मिजोरम के जनजातीय क्षेत्रों के लिए है। पंचायतों की शक्तियाँ 73वें संशोधन (अनुच्छेद 243) से संबंधित हैं। दल-बदल अयोग्यता दसवीं अनुसूची में है। भाषा संबंधी प्रावधान आठवीं अनुसूची में हैं।

question: Which of the following Articles allows the State to make special provisions for socially and educationally backward classes? (RPF Constable 2024 (07/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: Article 14 (5)
Article 15 (5)
Article 16 (5)
Article 17
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 15 (5)

Explanation:
Article 15 of the Indian Constitution prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth. However, Article 15 (5) allows the State to make special provisions for Socio-Educationally Backward Classes (SEBC), including admission to educational institutions. This clause was inserted by the 93rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2005. It enables reservation in government and private educational institutions (excluding minority institutions). Article 14 deals with equality before law, Article 16 ensures equality of opportunity in public employment, and Article 17 abolishes untouchability.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Which amendment added Article 15 (5)? → 93rd Constitutional Amendment (2005)
☛ For which classes does Article 15 (5) provide? → Socially and Educationally Backward Classes (SEBC)
☛ Which institutions are exempted from Article 15 (5)? → Minority educational institutions
☛ Article 15 (5) is related to? → Reservation in education
☛ Which article provides reservation in public employment? → Article 16 (4)
question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा अनुच्छेद राज्य को सामाजिक और शैक्षिक रूप से पिछड़े वर्गों के लिए विशेष प्रावधान करने की अनुमति देता है? (RPF Constable 2024 (07/03/2025) Shift 1)
options_hi: अनुच्छेद 14 (5)
अनुच्छेद 15 (5)
अनुच्छेद 16 (5)
अनुच्छेद 17
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है अनुच्छेद 15 (5)

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान का अनुच्छेद 15 धर्म, मूलवंश, जाति, लिंग या जन्म स्थान के आधार पर भेदभाव को प्रतिबंधित करता है। लेकिन अनुच्छेद 15 (5) राज्य को सामाजिक और शैक्षिक रूप से पिछड़े वर्गों (SEBC) के लिए शिक्षण संस्थानों में प्रवेश सहित विशेष प्रावधान करने की अनुमति देता है। यह प्रावधान 93वें संविधान संशोधन (2005) द्वारा जोड़ा गया था। इसके तहत सरकारी और निजी शैक्षणिक संस्थानों (अल्पसंख्यक संस्थानों को छोड़कर) में आरक्षण दिया जा सकता है। अनुच्छेद 14 समानता का अधिकार देता है, अनुच्छेद 16 सार्वजनिक रोजगार में अवसर की समानता से संबंधित है, और अनुच्छेद 17 अस्पृश्यता को समाप्त करता है।

question: Who among the following has the power to enforce the Fundamental Rights under Article 32? (RPF Constable 2024 (07/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: Supreme Court
Parliament
State Governments
President
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Supreme Court

Explanation:
The power to enforce Fundamental Rights under Article 32 lies with the Supreme Court. This Article is considered the 'soul of the Constitution' as it provides citizens the right to directly approach the Supreme Court in case of violation of Fundamental Rights. The Supreme Court can issue writs like Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari, and Quo Warranto for enforcement. Article 32 itself is a Fundamental Right and cannot be suspended except during a national emergency under Article 359.

☛ Who called Article 32 the 'soul of the Constitution'? → Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
☛ How many types of writs can be issued under Article 32? → 5
☛ Is Article 32 a Fundamental Right? → Yes
☛ When can Article 32 be suspended? → During national emergency

question: The list of all official languages is given in which Schedule of the Indian Constitution? (RPF Constable 2024 (07/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: Schedule 8
Schedule 7
Schedule 9
Schedule 10
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Schedule 8

Explanation:
The Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution contains the list of 22 official languages. These languages are included under Article 344(1) and 351 of the Constitution. Initially, the Eighth Schedule had only 14 languages, which were gradually increased to 22 through amendments. The 21st Amendment (1967) added Sindhi language. The 71st Amendment (1992) added Konkani, Manipuri, and Nepali. The 92nd Amendment (2003) added Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, and Santhali. This schedule forms the basis for the formation of the Official Language Commission and language-related policies in India.

question: Who is considered the de facto executive authority at the state level in India's parliamentary system? (RPF Constable 2024 (07/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: Chief Minister
Speaker of the Legislative Assembly
State Advocate General
Governor
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Chief Minister

Explanation:
In India's parliamentary system, the de facto executive authority at the state level is the Chief Minister. While the Governor is the constitutional (de jure) head, the Chief Minister is the real executive head (de facto). The Chief Minister leads the Council of Ministers and all state government decisions are taken in their name. This system is based on the British Westminster model, where actual executive power is exercised by the elected head of government. The Governor acts on the advice of the Chief Minister in most matters.

question: Which constitutional body is responsible for recommending principles for the allocation of grants-in-aid to states from the Consolidated Fund of India? (RPF Constable 2024 (07/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: Finance Commission
Planning Commission
NITI Aayog
National Development Council
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Finance Commission

Explanation:
According to Article 280 of the Indian Constitution, the Finance Commission is a constitutional body constituted by the President every five years. Its primary function is to recommend principles for the distribution of taxes between the Centre and the States and the allocation of grants-in-aid to states from the Consolidated Fund of India. The recommendations of the Finance Commission are not binding on the Parliament and state legislatures but are generally followed in practice. The first Finance Commission was formed in 1951, and so far 15 Finance Commissions have been constituted. The recommendations of the 16th Finance Commission are currently in effect. This commission plays a crucial role in balancing the financial position of states.

question: Which of the following Acts provided for the establishment of a federal, provincial and joint public service commission, Reserve Bank of India and a federal court? (RPF Constable 2024 (07/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: Government of India Act, 1919
Government of India Act, 1935
Government of India Act, 1929
Government of India Act, 1909
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Government of India Act, 1935

Explanation:
The Government of India Act, 1935 provided for the establishment of a federal, provincial and joint public service commission, the Reserve Bank of India, and a Federal Court. This act was designed to introduce a federal structure in India, granting greater autonomy to provinces. It also ended the system of diarchy at the provincial level and introduced provincial autonomy. The Federal Court was established as the apex court, which later became the Supreme Court. The Reserve Bank of India was also created under this act in 1935. The act was a significant step towards the constitutional development of India, though it was never fully implemented due to political opposition.

question: The Swaran Singh Committee, which recommended the inclusion of Fundamental Duties, was set up by whom among the following Indian Prime Ministers? (RPF Constable 2024 (07/03/2025) Shift 2)

Indira Gandhi

solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Indira Gandhi

Explanation:
The Swaran Singh Committee was set up in 1976 by the then Prime Minister Indira Gandhi. The committee, chaired by Sardar Swaran Singh, recommended the inclusion of Fundamental Duties in the Indian Constitution. Based on its recommendations, the 42nd Constitutional Amendment (1976) added the Fundamental Duties, which are enshrined in Article 51A under Part IVA. Initially, there were 10 duties, later increased to 11 by the 86th Amendment (2002). These duties outline the moral obligations of citizens and are considered essential for promoting patriotism and national unity.

question: Which of the following Amendment Acts provided one-third reservation for women in municipalities? (RPF Constable 2024 (07/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: 106th Amendment Act

solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 74th Amendment Act

Explanation:
The Indian Constitution's 74th Amendment Act, 1992 deals with municipalities. It added Part IX‑A and Articles 243‑P to 243‑ZG to the Constitution. It provides for one-third (33%) reservation of seats for women in all municipalities, including seats reserved for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes. The reservation also applies to the office of chairperson. The 73rd Amendment is related to Panchayati Raj institutions, while the 103rd Amendment provides reservation for Economically Weaker Sections (EWS). The 106th Amendment concerns women's reservation in Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies. Hence, the amendment that provided one-third reservation for women in municipalities is the 74th Amendment Act.

question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution declares that Directive Principles are NOT enforceable by any court? (RPF Constable 2024 (07/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: Article 35
Article 37
Article 45
Article 51
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 37

Explanation:
Article 37 of the Indian Constitution explicitly declares that the Directive Principles of State Policy are not enforceable by any court. This article states that these principles are fundamental in the governance of the country, but they cannot be challenged or enforced in a court of law. Their purpose is to guide the state in establishing social and economic justice. Article 35 empowers Parliament to make laws, Article 45 deals with early childhood care and education, and Article 51 promotes international peace and security. Unlike Fundamental Rights, Directive Principles are non-justiciable, meaning citizens cannot approach courts for their violation.

question: What is the primary function of the Cabinet in the Indian government? (RPF Constable 2024 (07/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: To manage only local government affairs
To act as the highest decision-making body in the formal sense
To conduct elections
To oversee international relations
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is To act as the highest decision-making body in the formal sense 

Explanation:
The Cabinet in India, comprising the Prime Minister and senior ministers, is the highest decision-making body of the government. It functions under Article 74 of the Constitution, which states that the President is bound by the advice of the Council of Ministers. The Cabinet makes policy decisions, approves bills, and coordinates administrative matters. It is not limited to local government, elections, or international relations but is responsible for national policy formulation and implementation. Thus, its primary function is to act as the supreme decision-making authority that drives the central government's functioning. The principle of collective responsibility ensures that all ministers support Cabinet decisions publicly.

question: Under which Act were Debt Recovery Tribunals (DRTs) established? (RPF Constable 2024 (07/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: The Recovery of Debts and Bankruptcy Act (RDB Act), 1993
The Securitization Act, 2002
The Consumer Protection Act, 2019
The SARFAESI Act, 2002
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The Recovery of Debts and Bankruptcy Act (RDB Act), 1993

Explanation:
Debt Recovery Tribunals (DRTs) were established under the Recovery of Debts and Bankruptcy Act (RDB Act), 1993. This act was enacted to expedite the recovery of debts due to banks and financial institutions. DRTs are constituted across India to adjudicate debt disputes involving amounts of ₹20 lakh or more. Later, in 2016, the act was amended and renamed as the 'Recovery of Debts and Bankruptcy Act' after merging with the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC). The SARFAESI Act, 2002, is a separate legislation dealing with securitization and reconstruction of financial assets.

question: The Preamble of the Indian Constitution was amended in 1976 to include which of the following words? (RPF Constable 2024 (07/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: Democratic and Republic
Unity and Integrity
Federal and Parliamentary
Socialist and Secular
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Socialist and Secular

Explanation:
The Preamble of the Indian Constitution was amended in 1976 by the 42nd Amendment to include the words 'Socialist', 'Secular', and 'Integrity'. Before the amendment, the Preamble described India as a 'Sovereign Democratic Republic'. After the amendment, it became a 'Sovereign Socialist Secular Democratic Republic'. Additionally, the phrase 'Unity of the Nation' was changed to 'Unity and Integrity of the Nation'. This amendment was passed during the Emergency under the government of Prime Minister Indira Gandhi. The word 'Socialist' emphasizes economic and social justice, while 'Secular' means the state maintains equal distance from all religions. These words reflect the fundamental character of the Indian state and its commitment to equality and justice. The 42nd Amendment is often called the 'Mini Constitution' due to the extensive changes it made.

☛ Is the Preamble a part of the Constitution? → Yes, as per Kesavananda Bharati case
☛ What does 'Secular' mean in the Preamble? → Equal treatment of all religions by the state

question: Who among the following appoints the Administrator of a Union Territory without a Legislative Assembly? (RPF Constable 2024 (07/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: Chief Minister of the State
The President of India
The Union Cabinet
The Prime Minister
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The President of India

Explanation:
According to Article 239 of the Indian Constitution, the administration of Union Territories without a Legislative Assembly is carried out by the President. The President appoints an Administrator for such Union Territories, who acts as the representative of the President. The Administrator holds office during the pleasure of the President. Examples of Union Territories without a Legislative Assembly include Chandigarh, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, Lakshadweep, and Andaman and Nicobar Islands. While the President acts on the advice of the Union Cabinet, the formal appointment is made by the President. The Chief Minister, Union Cabinet, or Prime Minister do not directly appoint the Administrator.

question: Which of the following Constitutional Amendment Acts has NOT inserted any Directive Principles of State Policy? (RPF Constable 2024 (07/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: 86th Constitutional Amendment Act
73rd Constitutional Amendment Act
42nd Constitutional Amendment Act
44th Constitutional Amendment Act
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act

Explanation:
The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act (1992) granted constitutional status to Panchayati Raj institutions but did not introduce any new Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP). In contrast, the 42nd Amendment (1976) added four new DPSPs: Article 39A (equal justice), 43A (participation in industry management), 46 (protection of SCs), and 48A (environment protection). The 44th Amendment (1978) amended Article 43. The 86th Amendment (2002) added Article 21A (right to education), which is a fundamental right, but also amended Article 45 (child education), which is a DPSP. Thus, only the 73rd Amendment does not relate to DPSP.

solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है 73वाँ संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम

Explanation:
73वाँ संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम (1992) ने पंचायती राज संस्थाओं को संवैधानिक दर्जा दिया, लेकिन इसमें राज्य के नीति निदेशक तत्व (DPSP) से संबंधित कोई नया अनुच्छेद नहीं जोड़ा गया। इसके विपरीत, 42वें संशोधन (1976) ने चार नए DPSP जोड़े: अनुच्छेद 39A (समान न्याय), 43A (उद्योग प्रबंधन में भागीदारी), 46 (अनुसूचित जातियों का संरक्षण) और 48A (पर्यावरण संरक्षण)। 44वें संशोधन (1978) ने अनुच्छेद 43 में संशोधन किया। 86वें संशोधन (2002) ने अनुच्छेद 21A (शिक्षा का अधिकार) जोड़ा, जो मौलिक अधिकार है, लेकिन अनुच्छेद 45 (बाल शिक्षा) को भी संशोधित किया, जो DPSP है। अतः केवल 73वाँ संशोधन DPSP से संबंधित नहीं है।

☛ भारत में DPSP की कुल संख्या → 25 (अनुच्छेद 36-51)

question: Which of the following were done by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act? (RPF Constable 2024 (07/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: Limiting the size of Council of Ministers.
Lowering the voting age from 21 to 18
Addition of word secular in the Preamble
Introducing the anti-defection law.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Addition of word secular in the Preamble

Explanation:
The 42nd Amendment (1976), known as the 'Mini-Constitution', added the words Socialist, Secular and Integrity to the Preamble. Limiting the size of the Council of Ministers was done by the 91st Amendment (2003). Lowering the voting age from 21 to 18 was done by the 61st Amendment (1988). The anti-defection law was introduced by the 52nd Amendment (1985). Therefore, only the addition of 'secular' in the Preamble is a work of the 42nd Amendment.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Words added to Preamble by 42nd Amendment → Socialist, Secular, Integrity
☛ Amendment limiting size of Council of Ministers → 91st Amendment (2003)
☛ Amendment lowering voting age to 18 → 61st Amendment (1988)
☛ Amendment related to anti-defection law → 52nd Amendment (1985)
☛ 42nd Amendment is also known as → Mini-Constitution
question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा कार्य 42वें संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम द्वारा किया गया था? (RPF Constable 2024 (07/03/2025) Shift 3)
options_hi: मंत्रिपरिषद के आकार को सीमित करना।
मतदान की आयु 21 से घटाकर 18 करना
प्रस्तावना में 'धर्मनिरपेक्ष' शब्द जोड़ना
दल-बदल विरोधी कानून लागू करना।
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है प्रस्तावना में 'धर्मनिरपेक्ष' शब्द जोड़ना

Explanation:
42वें संशोधन (1976) को 'मिनी-संविधान' कहा जाता है। इसने प्रस्तावना में समाजवादी, धर्मनिरपेक्ष और अखंडता शब्द जोड़े। मंत्रिपरिषद के आकार को सीमित करना 91वें संशोधन (2003) द्वारा किया गया। मतदान की आयु 21 से 18 करना 61वें संशोधन (1988) द्वारा हुआ। दल-बदल विरोधी कानून 52वें संशोधन (1985) द्वारा जोड़ा गया। अतः केवल प्रस्तावना में धर्मनिरपेक्ष जोड़ना 42वें संशोधन का कार्य है।

☛ 42वें संशोधन द्वारा प्रस्तावना में जोड़े गए शब्द → समाजवादी, धर्मनिरपेक्ष, अखंडता
☛ मंत्रिपरिषद के आकार को सीमित करने वाला संशोधन → 91वां संशोधन (2003)
☛ मतदान आयु 18 वर्ष करने वाला संशोधन → 61वां संशोधन (1988)
☛ दल-बदल विरोधी कानून से संबंधित संशोधन → 52वां संशोधन (1985)
☛ 42वें संशोधन को कहा जाता है → मिनी-संविधान

question: Who appoints the Chairman of National Green Tribunal? (RPF Constable 2024 (07/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: He/She is appointed by the Central Government.
He/She is appointed by the Home Minister
He/She is appointed by the Chief Justice of India.
He/She is appointed by the State Government.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is He/She is appointed by the Central Government.

Explanation:
The National Green Tribunal (NGT) was established in 2010 under the National Green Tribunal Act. The Chairman of NGT is appointed by the Central Government in consultation with the Chief Justice of India and other senior judges. The Chairman must be a Judge of a High Court. NGT is responsible for the speedy disposal of environmental disputes. The tenure of the Chairman is 5 years or until the age of 70 years, whichever is earlier.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ When was the National Green Tribunal established? → 2010
☛ What is the minimum qualification for NGT Chairman? → Judge of a High Court
☛ What is the tenure of NGT Chairman? → 5 years or 70 years of age
☛ Under which act was NGT formed? → National Green Tribunal Act
☛ In consultation with whom is the NGT Chairman appointed? → Chief Justice of India
question_hi: राष्ट्रीय हरित अधिकरण के अध्यक्ष की नियुक्ति कौन करता है? (RPF Constable 2024 (07/03/2025) Shift 3)
options_hi: उनकी नियुक्ति केंद्र सरकार द्वारा की जाती है।
उनकी नियुक्ति गृह मंत्री द्वारा की जाती है।
उनकी नियुक्ति भारत के मुख्य न्यायाधीश द्वारा की जाती है।
उनकी नियुक्ति राज्य सरकार द्वारा की जाती है।
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है उनकी नियुक्ति केंद्र सरकार द्वारा की जाती है।

Explanation:
राष्ट्रीय हरित अधिकरण (NGT) की स्थापना वर्ष 2010 में राष्ट्रीय हरित अधिकरण अधिनियम के तहत की गई थी। इसके अध्यक्ष की नियुक्ति भारत की केंद्र सरकार द्वारा भारत के मुख्य न्यायाधीश और अन्य वरिष्ठ न्यायाधीशों के परामर्श से की जाती है। अध्यक्ष को उच्च न्यायालय का न्यायाधीश होना अनिवार्य है। NGT का मुख्य उद्देश्य पर्यावरण संबंधी विवादों का त्वरित निपटारा करना है। अध्यक्ष का कार्यकाल 5 वर्ष या 70 वर्ष की आयु तक होता है।
